clue.text: Pass on corner by busy road, heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means the joined letters are read from right to left

parts.note: to corner someone is to trap them
the M1 is Britain's busiest motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Directions telling someone to go on past a corner beside a busy road and then turn west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' turns the whole run TRAPMI. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds, its 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart news is to communicate it, handing it on to someone else.

clue.text: Everyone will be up for such a recruitment drive

definitions.text: Everyone will be up for such a recruitment drive

parts.words: Everyone will be up for such a recruitment drive
parts.note: reads as a jobs drive everyone is keen on, but also suggests the early delivery round of a dairyman, for which everyone rises at dawn

explanation.surface: A hiring campaign so attractive that every candidate is keen to join.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the annual tour of universities by employers seeking graduates is named after the dairyman's early-morning delivery round.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is the British name for the yearly campus recruitment tour by big employers.

clue.text: Knowing route in part of London

parts.note: an arch look is a knowing, sly one
a way is a route

explanation.surface: Someone streetwise knows the best path through a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The district is in north London. 'Knowing' here is an adjective meaning sly, as in an arch smile.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names a district in north London, in the borough of Islington.

clue.text: Flap when strike's coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to bat is to strike, as with a bat; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A flag goes up when a strike is about to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tab is a small flap or tag attached to something, used for pulling or labelling.

clue.text: Fin-de-siècle poster in suitable setting

indicators.note: the poster sits inside the word for suitable, which forms its setting

parts.note: decent means suitable or acceptable
an ad, or advertisement, is a poster

explanation.surface: A turn-of-the-century poster displayed in a fitting frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' tells you the suitable word surrounds the poster.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for the late nineteenth century describes an age of decay, so it serves as an adjective for self-indulgent decline.

clue.text: South America's cooking pot

definitions.meaning: the name for the southern states of the USA, the American South
a large iron pot used by soldiers for cooking or making tea

explanation.surface: A cooking pot belonging to South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America's' looks like the continent, but it means the South of America, the old Confederate states.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a nickname for the US South and British military slang for a field kettle.

clue.text: Shrub taken from bed over holiday period

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
on can mean over, as in a lid on a pot
Easter is a holiday period in spring

explanation.surface: A bush was dug up from a flower bed during the spring holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' looks like a garden bed, which suits a shrub, but it is a child's cot.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant is a common garden shrub with small leaves and red berries.

clue.text: Like fellow, perhaps, outside pub flipping coins?

indicators.note: the money word goes around the turned pub, outside it

parts.note: dosh is British slang for money

indicators.note: flipping means the word for a pub is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Someone tosses coins outside a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like it goes with coins being tossed, but it turns the pub word round. A fellow is a senior member of an Oxford or Cambridge college, also called a don.
explanation.definitionFit: Donnish means scholarly and bookish, in the manner of a university teacher such as a fellow.

clue.text: Batty woman getting married in Bellini work

indicators.note: the letter for married goes in the woman's name

parts.note: Nora Batty is a famous character from the British TV comedy Last of the Summer Wine

explanation.surface: A crazy woman marries in the middle of a Bellini opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batty' looks like an adjective meaning mad, but it is a surname: Nora Batty, the wrinkled-stockinged neighbour in Last of the Summer Wine, a long-running British sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of Bellini's best-known opera, about a Druid priestess.

clue.text: Ban TV item revealing how Jumbo killed people?

definitions.text: item revealing how Jumbo killed people?

parts.note: to black something is to boycott or ban it, as a union might
the box is a slang name for television

explanation.surface: A banned television set somehow shows how an elephant killed people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' looks like an elephant but is a jumbo jet; the item is the flight recorder recovered after a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight recorder is examined after an air crash to show what caused it.

clue.text: Rejection of rather unethical housing term

indicators.note: rejection suggests throwing back, so the found letters are read backwards
of means the letters come out of the following words, taken from within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A landlord rejects lease conditions as rather unethical.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft gave the hidden run no indicator; 'of' does that job, taking letters out of 'rather unethical', and 'Rejection' turns ERUNET round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenure is the period or terms on which a home is held, such as freehold or leasehold.

clue.text: It's common, after King or Queen, to see Jack played here

indicators.note: after places the common land word behind the royal word

parts.note: the Crown stands for the monarch, king or queen
a green is a village common

explanation.surface: A village green is a place to watch Jack, after the monarch, play.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack is the small white target ball in lawn bowls, not a playing card. This is a British bowling lawn raised in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bowling lawn, higher in the centre, where the game aimed at the jack is played.

clue.text: Go off with person, say, to find cheap place to eat

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone bad and are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: Leave with someone to find a cheap café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' looks like 'leave', but 'off' is the anagram signal working on GO, PERSON and SAY together.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang term for a cheap, grubby café serving fried food.

clue.text: Current leadership, Russian, say

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
the van is the vanguard, the leading position

explanation.surface: The present leadership is Russian, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests present-day, but it is the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A very common Russian man's name, so a typical Russian.

clue.text: Landing-place of great importance announced

indicators.note: announced says a word is spoken, so its sound matters, not its spelling

parts.note: key means of great importance, as in a key issue

explanation.surface: A landing-place of great importance is formally proclaimed.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a stone platform where boats tie up and unload.

clue.text: Doctor being rash closing a lengthy speech

indicators.note: closing means the scrambled letters close around, enclosing, the following word
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A medic's careless haste ends a long talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician, but it is the anagram signal on BEING RASH; 'closing' puts that round A.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a long, tiresome harangue that someone has to sit through.

clue.text: New York bread lines heading east

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, the lines

indicators.note: heading means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Railway lines in New York run east.
explanation.walkthrough: RY, for railway, is a crossword convention for 'lines'.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark grain bread is a famous staple of New York delis.

clue.text: Not able to feel calm and collected

definitions.meaning: showing no nervousness, cool under pressure

explanation.surface: Someone numb to feeling yet perfectly composed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerveless means both literally lacking nerves and figuratively unshaken by fear.

clue.text: Tight net closed on a teenager

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A taut net was drawn shut on a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' looks like it describes the net, but it is slang for drunk, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person between childhood and adulthood, roughly a teenager.

clue.text: Preventing recall of article in list

indicators.note: the article is placed in the word for list

parts.note: a ship that lists leans to one side
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An article in a list stops something being recalled, like a faulty product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recall' suggests a product recall, but it means memory: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethean describes what brings oblivion, causing forgetfulness, after the mythical river.

clue.text: Part of Koran or Buddhist scripture that's timeless

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: a sutra is a Buddhist or Hindu scripture

explanation.surface: A passage from one holy book or another that lasts for ever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' looks like praise for scripture but removes T.
explanation.definitionFit: A sura is one of the chapters of the Koran.

clue.text: Drive dangerously and argue — it's the way of many drunks

parts.note: to skid is to slide out of control on the road
to row is to argue

explanation.surface: Reckless driving and quarrels are typical of heavy drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the run-down street of a city where vagrants and alcoholics gather; 'way' is a street.
explanation.definitionFit: A city area where down-and-outs and alcoholics live rough.

clue.text: Left rather short

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: quite means rather, as in quite good

explanation.surface: Departed somewhat early.
explanation.definitionFit: As a past tense, quit means left, departed from a place.

clue.text: Drug's the first excluded from meal

indicators.note: the first letter of the meal word is left out

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: Drugs are the first thing banned at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper is slang for a stimulant drug such as amphetamine.

clue.text: Terribly solemn sorts can make dire bosses

indicators.note: can make says these letters can be reworked to form something else

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Grim managers turn out to be very serious people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' signals the anagram of DIRE BOSSES.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobersides is a humourless, staid person, so the plural means solemn types.

clue.text: Bust of poet who gave up one of his Os

indicators.note: gave up means a letter is surrendered from the poet's name

parts.note: Rupert Brooke was an English poet of the First World War
the poet's name contains two letter Os, and one goes

explanation.surface: A sculpted head of a poet who sacrificed something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like a sculpture but is the definition meaning penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: Bust and broke both mean having no money left.

clue.text: Notice fare includes parking ——- one gives you the going rate

definitions.text: one gives you the going rate

indicators.note: includes means the joined words hold the parking letter within them

parts.note: to see is to notice
to do is to fare, as in how do you do

explanation.surface: Notice that the fee covers parking, which sets the rate charged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going rate' looks like a price, but it means speed: the instrument shows how fast you go.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedometer, informally shortened, displays the rate at which a vehicle is moving.

clue.text: Possible rating to be given when successful with aims?

definitions.text: Possible rating to be given when successful with aims?

parts.words: Possible rating to be given when successful with aims?
parts.note: reads as a performance grade, but a marksman who hits the bullseye has aims that score on the board

explanation.surface: A grade awarded when goals are achieved.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means accurate or succeeding, as a shot that hits the bullseye.

clue.text: Sheep do this after sleeping?

parts.note: what one does after sleep is get up, and in a down entry those letters going up read backwards

explanation.surface: Asks what sheep do when they wake.
explanation.walkthrough: A teg is a sheep in its second year; get, written upwards in a down light, reads as its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A teg is a two-year-old sheep, a dialect and farming word.

clue.text: Arsenal's big guns passing round new yellow ball

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow

indicators.note: passing round means the yellow ball words wrap around the letter for new

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Arsenal's star players pass the new yellow football around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arsenal' looks like the London football club, with its big guns as star players, but an arsenal is a weapons store.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordnance means artillery, the heavy guns kept in an arsenal.

clue.text: Is Parisian short dress first to be destroyed?

indicators.note: first puts the dress piece at the front of the answer
short means the dress word loses its last letter

parts.note: a gown is a dress
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A Paris fashion query: is the short frock to be thrown out first?
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is an idiom for being lost or ruined, as things are said to vanish westwards with the setting sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be lost, wrecked or killed, so it equals being destroyed.
